newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Mispec says unfairly tarnished by Busang.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Mispec says unfairly tarnished by Busang.

text.p: Canada's junior gold mining companies have been unfairly tarnished by association with Bre-X Minerals Ltd, and that company's problems with the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia, the president of Mispec Resources Inc said in an interview with Reuters.

"The Bre-X situation, which everybody is now being compared to, was really a three legged stool - first there was a title problem, then it became a political interference issue, and now it is regulatory problem," said Harold Jackson, president of Mispec Resources, a Montreal-listed explorer which is also exploring for gold in Indonesia.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd, the small Alberta-based mining company that found Busang, shocked the mining world last month by announcing that the amount of gold at Busang might be significantly less than originally estimated. Bre-X had earlier put Busang's gold reserves at 70.95 million ounces, which would have made it one of the finds of the century.
The results of an independent audit by Canadian consultants Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd are expected in the next few weeks.
But as a result on March 27 Bre-X shares collapsed from around C$12.00 a share to less than $2.00.

On the same day the Vancouver Stock Exchange's Resource Index fell 6.8 percent to 2,013.28, and the gold component of the Toronto Stock Exchange 300 composite index fell 8.7 percent to 9,559.92, the largest one day decline since September 7,1993.
Mispec Resources shares fell from C$3.00 to around C$1.80 and are currently trading around C$1.85 a share.

Mispec Resources is exploring the Jampany property in the western portion of the Indonesian island of Java, 150 kilometres south of the capital, Jakarta, in a joint venture with Indonesian company, Hunamas Putra Interbuana, a private Indonesian company.
Mispec Resources has never had any of the political or regulatory problems that Bre-X had, Jackson argued.

"Indonesia's laws in regard to mining are not onerous," Jackson said. "The laws are clearly written by geologists for geologists and have been translated into English, and to stay onside is relatively simple," he said.

"One of the things that makes Mispec unusual is that it existed as a shell and this Indonesian property came looking for a structure to put itself into, so our Indonesian partners came looking for us, not the other way around," Jackson said.
The vice-chairman of Indonesia's Institute of Science (LIPI), Dr S. Suparka, sits on Mispec's board.

"Secondly, the property is on Java where KP's rule," he said. "KPs are mining rights given to Indonesians, not foreigners, but the laws are structured in a manner that you can have a working interest in a KP thru the Indonesian partner, so title is a lot clearer."

"Unlike Bre-X no 'contract of work' is needed by Mispec, as the KP gives you step-by-step authorization to automatically move forward into mining, with an environmental permit and building permit," he said.

Thirdly, Mispec's exploration site was chosen because surveys by Dutch geologists in the 1930's showed potential and because the site had been focused on by the Indonesian Institute of Science and Technology (LIPI), he said.
Comprising a total area of 20,530 hectares, the property is divided into two contiguous blocks: the Jampang (9,805 ha) and Jampang East (10,725 ha).
Mispec has a 30 percent interest in Jampang and an option to earn up to 90 percent, while in Jampang East Mispec has a 65 percent interest, which can be increased to 85 percent.
Mispec has been concentrating on Jampang where last July it launched a $2 million 26,000 metre drill program to test the potential of the LIPI epithermal gold prospect.
So far a near-surface resource of 2.5 million tonnes, grading 3.11 grams of gold per tonne, has been calculated.
All sample preparation and assaying is being carried out by Inchcape Testing Services in Jakarta, the leading assay laboratory in Indonesia, Jackson said.
Mispec's property lies immediately adjacent to the Pongkor gold mine which currently produces 100,000 ounces of gold annually.

"Mispec is adequately funded to complete its exploration program into 1998, so we are not interested in a stock promotion, we are only interested in our stock price reflecting underlying asset value," Jackson said.
Mispec has 35 million shares on issue, on a fully diluted basis, of which management owns 2.9 million and there is a free float of 20 million.

Until the Busang affair, Canadian mining companies had a good record in finding major mineral deposits in recent years, including the Arequipa in Peru and Voisey Bay in Canada, and Toronto became a center for mining finance as a result, analysts said.

"In 1996 a total of US$6.5 billion was raised in Canada (for the mining industry) either through various lending arrangements, commodity-backed financing, or through the issuance of debt and equity," said Jeffrey Christian, managing director of New York-based industry consultants, CPM Group.
On a comparative basis, last year $1.5 billion was raised for the mining industry in Australia, followed by $1.4 billion in New York and $1.3 billion in Johannesburg, he said.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641
